dossier.architecture: Compliant floor pickup and rotating dual-piece effector on continuous elevator.

subsystems.drivetrain: WCP Swerve XS; steering motor adaptation described in interview, exact model transcription unresolved.
subsystems.intake: Compliant four-bar folds rearward; reverse roller action deploys pickup.
subsystems.transfer: Funnel orients coral into rotating effector.
subsystems.scoring: Two-stage continuous elevator; shaped algae wheels retain ball during rotation and support net launch while also manipulating coral.
subsystems.endgame: Recently added RI3D/Orbit-like harness and winch; deployment follows intake stow.
subsystems.controls: Three Limelights, tag alignment and piece localization; interview distinguishes four-coral autonomous goal from reported two/three average.

versions: Climber was a recent addition at filming.
Do not record four-piece goal as established typical autonomous output.
dossier.analysis: Set autonomous requirements as a distribution of reliable outcomes. A team reporting an average of two or three should not be indexed as an automatic four-piece robot simply because four was the target.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-180 · Self-deploying acquisition still requires indexed possession
context_documents.body:
# 2025-180: Self-deploying acquisition still requires indexed possession

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A compliant four-bar floor collector feeds a funnel and rotating effector on a two-stage continuous elevator. The retained interview describes reverse roller action deploying the collector. One collector sensor and three arm sensors manage entry, indexing and retention; camera-based acquisition chooses a robot pose relative to the pickup.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team connects floor pickup to shorter coral cycles and describes automatic reef-facing behavior as a way to streamline the driver’s next scoring action. It sought both task-related and climb ranking points.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Passive or roller-driven deployment reduces a dedicated actuator but makes friction, game-piece contact and the initial mechanism state part of the deployment logic. Multiple sensors provide intermediate possession states instead of equating “something entered” with “ready to score.” A combined coral/algae mechanism must also preserve the retained object through rotation, not just when stationary.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test partial handoffs, skewed coral, deployment without a piece, and failures of each sensor. Verify motor identifiers in CAD/code because automatic captions corrupt model names.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sgTeheZy33I](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sgTeheZy33I)

source_reviews.title: S.P.A.M. 2025 public robot code
source_reviews.locator: README, RobotContainer, Auto, IntakeCoral, elevatorArm, elevatorArmAlgae and climber Java packages
source_reviews.review_basis: Read controller bindings, real hardware I/O and transition logic in public snapshot
facts: Floor intake, indexer and arm sensors coordinate handoff. Station feeds in reverse at a separate receiving pose. Cage capture and winch have separate motor commands and two digital latch inputs.
limitations: Code establishes configuration and commanded behavior, with no measurement of physical geometry or event-specific deployment.

source_reviews.title: FRC 180 S.P.A.M. 2025 Code Release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team release and technical follow-up
facts: The one-driver setup led to cross-subsystem triggers. Dynamic floor coral targeting shifted most motion toward DriveToPose, and simulation was used for early driver practice and logic validation.
limitations: Team reports simulation and field use without publishing a timed comparison or reliability dataset.

subsystems.name: Floor acquisition and coral registration
subsystems.construction: Pivoted intake with separate bottom-roller command, LaserCan, driven indexer and three discrete inputs on the arm tool.
subsystems.operation: Gate the transfer on receiver pose, stage at the arm, and suppress coral deployment while a piece is entering. The arm also has passive indexing as a default command.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team described coordinating many subsystems centrally for one driver. Haptic feedback tells the driver when floor coral is acquired.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The intake sensor can justify driving away from the pickup sooner than arm staging alone. Keep downstream release gated separately so an intake detection cannot be mistaken for a scoring-ready piece.
subsystems.interfaces: Intake sensor to autonomous transition, indexer to arm, and receiving height and angle.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test out-of-order sensor events, stalled transfer and damage to the bottom-roller mount. Rumble reports software state and should be checked against physical possession.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller contact geometry, material, preload and station funnel geometry.

subsystems.name: Scoring and dynamic alignment
subsystems.construction: Elevator, arm pivot, coral and algae drive channels, and camera-based target selection. Algae tool I/O includes a CANrange.
subsystems.operation: Branch and level input select a reef target. Auto combines pose-based travel to a seen floor piece with separate scoring and intake triggers. PathPlanner retains the curved exit from the first score.
subsystems.team_rationale: Most moves were straight or depended on observed piece positions. The team used simulation to reuse behavior across teleop and auto and used field time to refine vision and auto-align.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Target-dependent motion cuts dead travel if detection is timely. Occlusion and erroneous detection can erase that gain, so test with clutter and partially visible reef tags.
subsystems.interfaces: Camera to drivetrain target, drivetrain tolerance to scoring, and lift and pivot release geometry.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check for alignment timeouts, camera dropout and interrupted scoring reset. Team reports pulsed rumble for slow alignment and separate completion feedback.
subsystems.unknowns: Field-calibrated pose tolerances across events, mechanical lift rigging and tool dimensions.

subsystems.name: Cage capture and lift
subsystems.construction: Separate Talon FX outputs for winch and grabber, absolute position feedback and two digital inputs.
subsystems.operation: Deployment advances to a position threshold. In deployed state the grabber runs until both sensors have tripped and cleared. A separate driver command winches toward the climb limit.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team used distinct rumbles for deployed and latched conditions because the mechanism is difficult to see from the driver station.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Two completed sensor transitions can distinguish entry from settled engagement. Confirm that a skewed cage or bounce cannot produce the same sequence with poor retention.
subsystems.interfaces: Grabber inputs to capture confirmation, winch feedback to travel limit, and climb pose to arm and floor-intake clearance.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check sensor sequence, mount alignment and load holding after disable, which motor neutral mode alone cannot establish.
subsystems.unknowns: Physical hook and retention geometry, winch reeving, cage load path and proof test.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Anemone coordinates a floor intake and intermediate indexer with a coral roller tool on a pivoting elevator arm. The lift and arm also present an independently driven algae tool. A station receive pose runs the coral tool in reverse, providing another supply path. The one-driver interface can align to a branch while issuing lift and pivot commands. Late in the match, a separate powered cage capture and winch operate while the elevator, arm and floor intake move into climb-specific positions.
source_review.piece_flow: For floor coral, the code moves the lift to stow, extends the intake and sets the arm to receive. Once lift and arm are ready it starts the indexer and intake on the arm. An intake LaserCan detects a piece, and three arm inputs distinguish partial, entering and staged coral. The intake stops feeding once coral enters the arm. Station input commands reverse intake and indexing with the arm at a different height and angle. Coral is released at the selected branch or L1 pose. The code also exposes reef algae removal, floor or lollipop pickup poses, and processor and barge modes through the arm's algae tool.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Elevator height, arm pivot and floor-intake deployment must agree before coral crosses the handoff gap. The code also uses a closer reef deployment gate in situations where the arm can block a vision target. The resulting motion constraint is partly optical. A pose can clear the reef physically and still obscure the camera needed to finish lining up. In climb mode the arm and elevator take separate positions while the coral intake uses an extreme-stow command.
revisions: Team documents a shift from broader PathPlanner use to dynamic DriveToPose with a retained first-exit curve. Hardware installation dates remain unresolved in the released code.
transferable_principles: Treat early piece detection and scoring-ready confirmation as different states. Simulate trigger ordering and validate contact and occlusion on a real field.
disconfirming_conditions: Dynamic pickup loses value if the first reliable piece observation arrives late, alignment is often obstructed, or the handoff prevents driving away promptly.
remaining_gaps: Mechanical drawing and dimensional review, event-specific software revisions, cage retention hardware and field cycle distributions.
recommended_images: Team code-release post 1 for the labeled Anemone overview.
AdvantageScope simulation illustration in the same post for state visualization, explicitly identified as simulation.
